{"kind":"tool","id":"TXCPmm1dSgY","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"DATABASE_DESIGN.md","instructions":"Write the database design documentation","content":"# Database Design — Community Food Donation and Distribution System

Database: **MongoDB** (document store) accessed through **Mongoose ODM**.
If `MONGODB_URI` is empty the server boots a temporary in-memory MongoDB for
development/demos — the same schemas and queries are used unchanged.

---

## 1. Entity Relationship Overview

```
User (DONOR) 1 ──── * Donation * ──── 1 User (NGO)
                      │  │
                      │  └─────── * ──── 1 User (VOLUNTEER)   (assignedVolunteerId)
                      │
                      ├──── 1 Pickup (1 active per donation)
                      │        └── volunteerId → User (VOLUNTEER)
                      │
                      └──── * DonationHistory  (immutable audit trail)

User 1 ──── * Notification   (per-recipient in-app notifications)
```

Five collections (Mongoose models):

| Model | File | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `User` | `server/models/User.js` | All four roles in one collection, discriminated by `role` |
| `Donation` | `server/models/Donation.js` | A surplus-food listing and its lifecycle state |
| `Pickup` | `server/models/Pickup.js` | Pickup/delivery task linking a donation, NGO and volunteer |
| `DonationHistory` | `server/models/DonationHistory.js` | Append-only audit trail of every status change |
| `Notification` | `server/models/Notification.js` | In-app notifications per user |

---

## 2. Collections

### 2.1 `users`

One collection for every role; `role` selects which optional profile fields matter.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `name` | String | 2–100 chars |
| `email` | String | unique, lowercase, indexed |
| `passwordHash` | String | bcrypt, **`select: false`**, stripped in `toJSON` |
| `phone` | String | validated pattern |
| `role` | String enum | `DONOR`, `NGO`, `VOLUNTEER`, `ADMIN` |
| `address` | String | optional |
| `city` | String | required, indexed with role |
| `organizationName` | String | NGO profile |
| `organizationDescription` | String | NGO profile |
| `verificationStatus` | String enum | `NOT_REQUIRED`, `PENDING`, `VERIFIED`, `REJECTED` — NGOs start `PENDING` |
| `verificationNote` | String | admin's note when verifying/rejecting |
| `donorCategory` | String enum | Household, Restaurant, Hotel, Hostel, College Canteen, Event Organizer, Catering Service, Other |
| `isActive` | Boolean | admin can deactivate an account (login and access blocked) |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | Date | Mongoose timestamps |

Indexes: `{ email: 1 }` (unique), `{ city: 1, role: 1 }`, `{ role: 1, isActive: 1 }`.

### 2.2 `donations`

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `foodName` | String | ≤120 |
| `category` | String enum | Cooked Meals, Fruits, Vegetables, Bakery Products, Packaged Food, Rice and Grains, Other |
| `description` | String | ≤2000 |
| `quantity` | Number | >0 |
| `unit` | String enum | Servings, Kg, Plates, Packs, Boxes, Litres, Dozen |
| `foodClassification` | String enum | `VEG`, `NON_VEG`, `BOTH` |
| `preparationDate` | Date | when the food was prepared |
| `availableFrom` | Date | when pickup can start |
| `safeConsumptionDeadline` | Date | **required** — expired donations are never eligible for acceptance |
| `pickupAddress`, `city` | String | required pickup location |
| `locationDescription` | String | landmarks etc. |
| `storageInformation` | String | how the food is stored |
| `additionalNotes` | String | free text |
| `contactName`, `contactPhone` | String | required contact details |
| `imageUrl` | String | Multer upload path (optional) |
| `donorId` | ObjectId → User | required, indexed |
| `acceptedByNgoId` | ObjectId → User | set on acceptance; guarantees single-NGO acceptance |
| `assignedVolunteerId` | ObjectId → User | set when a volunteer takes the task |
| `status` | String enum | see lifecycle below; default `AVAILABLE` |
| `statusUpdatedAt` | Date | last transition time |
| `statusUpdatedBy` | ObjectId → User | who made the last transition |
| `distributionNote` | String | NGO's note when confirming distribution |
| `cancelledReason` | String | on cancel/reject |

Status lifecycle (`server/utils/statusFlow.js` — single source of truth, validated on
every transition):

```
AVAILABLE → ACCEPTED → PICKUP_ASSIGNED → COLLECTED → DISTRIBUTED → COMPLETED
     ↘ CANCELLED / REJECTED
```

`COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`, `REJECTED` are terminal. Acceptance eligibility =
`status === AVAILABLE` **and** `safeConsumptionDeadline >= now`.

Indexes: `{ donorId: 1 }`, `{ acceptedByNgoId: 1 }`, `{ assignedVolunteerId: 1 }`,
`{ status: 1, safeConsumptionDeadline: 1 }`, `{ city: 1 }`, `{ createdAt: -1 }`.

Concurrency safety: the accept operation performs an atomic conditional update
(`findOneAndUpdate` with `status: AVAILABLE` + non-expired deadline in the filter),
so two NGOs racing on the same donation can never both succeed — the loser receives `409`.

### 2.3 `pickups`

One **active** pickup task per donation (`isActive: true`); released volunteers
return the task to `OPEN`.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `donationId` | ObjectId → Donation | required, indexed |
| `ngoId` | ObjectId → User | the accepting NGO |
| `volunteerId` | ObjectId → User | nullable until a volunteer accepts |
| `pickupAddress`, `deliveryAddress` | String | copied from the donation / NGO profile |
| `scheduledPickupTime` | Date | optional |
| `assignmentDate` | Date | default now |
| `status` | String enum | `OPEN`, `ASSIGNED`, `COLLECTED`, `DELIVERED`, `CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED` |
| `collectedAt`, `deliveredAt`, `confirmedAt` | Date | event timestamps |
| `notes` | String | volunteer's collection notes |
| `deliveryNotes` | String | volunteer's delivery notes |
| `isActive` | Boolean | one active task per donation |

Indexes: `{ donationId: 1, isActive: 1 }`, `{ volunteerId: 1 }`, `{ ngoId: 1 }`, `{ status: 1 }`.

The pickup status mirrors the donation status (collect → `COLLECTED` on both,
deliver → donation `DISTRIBUTED`, NGO confirm → pickup `CONFIRMED` + donation `COMPLETED`).

### 2.4 `donationhistories`

Append-only audit trail — rows are **never updated or deleted**.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `donationId` | ObjectId → Donation | required, indexed |
| `previousStatus` | String | null for the first entry |
| `newStatus` | String | required |
| `updatedBy` | ObjectId → User | who performed the transition |
| `updatedByRole` | String | snapshot for easy filtering |
| `note` | String | optional context (delivery notes, admin reason…) |
| `timestamp` | Date | default now |

Index: `{ donationId: 1, timestamp: 1 }`.
The donor, NGO and admin detail pages all render this trail, so every status change
is fully traceable — key for the platform's accountability goal.

### 2.5 `notifications`

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `userId` | ObjectId → User | recipient, indexed |
| `title` | String | ≤120 |
| `message` | String | ≤500 |
| `type` | String enum | `INFO`, `SUCCESS`, `WARNING`, `DONATION`, `PICKUP`, `ACCOUNT` |
| `relatedDonationId` | ObjectId → Donation | nullable deep link |
| `isRead` | Boolean | default false, indexed |

Index: `{ userId: 1, isRead: 1, createdAt: -1 }`.

---

## 3. Design Decisions

1. **Single `users` collection** — the four roles share authentication/profile fields;
   role-specific data lives in optional fields. Simple for a student project, and
   querying "all NGOs in Pune" is one indexed query.
2. **Status as data, transitions as code** — the state machine lives in
   `utils/statusFlow.js`; controllers validate every transition against it, so an
   illegal jump (e.g. `COMPLETED → AVAILABLE`) is impossible regardless of the caller.
3. **Immutable audit trail** — `donationhistories` is insert-only; the current state
   lives on the donation, the story lives in the trail.
4. **Atomic acceptance** — conditional `findOneAndUpdate` prevents the classic
   double-accept race without needing distributed locks.
5. **Denormalized pickup copy** — pickup/delivery addresses are copied onto the task
   so the volunteer sees exactly what the donor registered even if the listing changes.
6. **Security by default** — `passwordHash` is `select: false`, stripped from JSON
   output, and never returned by any endpoint.

/** GET /api/ngo/donations  (NGO) - available donations with filters. */
const browseDonations = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const restrictToAvailable = !req.query.status || req.query.status === DONATION_STATUS.AVAILABLE;
  const { filter, sort, page, limit, skip } = buildDonationQuery(req.query, {
    restrictToAvailable,
    includeExpired: req.query.includeExpired === 'true',
  });

  const [items, total] = await Promise.all([
    Donation.find(filter).sort(sort).skip(skip).limit(limit).lean(),
    Donation.countDocuments(filter),
  ]);

  return ok(res, {
    donations: items.map((d) => ({ ...d, isExpired: isExpired(d) })),
    pagination: { page, limit, total, pages: Math.ceil(total / limit) || 1 },
  });
});

/**
 * POST /api/ngo/donations/:id/accept  (NGO)
 * Concurrency-safe: the conditional update only succeeds while the donation
 * is still AVAILABLE, so two NGOs can never accept the same donation.
 */
const acceptDonation = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const donation = await loadDonationForNgo(req.params.id, req.user);

  if (isExpired(donation)) {
    throw ApiError.badRequest('This donation is past its safe-consumption deadline and can no longer be accepted');
  }

  let accepted;
  try {
    // Conditional update: only succeeds while the donation is still AVAILABLE,
    // which is what prevents two NGOs from accepting the same donation.
    accepted = await transitionDonation({
      donationId: donation._id,
      fromStatus: DONATION_STATUS.AVAILABLE,
      toStatus: DONATION_STATUS.ACCEPTED,
      user: req.user,
      note: `Accepted by ${req.user.organizationName || req.user.name}`,
      extraUpdate: { acceptedByNgoId: req.user._id },
    });
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.statusCode === 409) throw ApiError.conflict('This donation has already been accepted by another NGO');
    throw err;
  }

  await notify({
    recipientId: accepted.donorId,
    title: 'Donation accepted',
    message: `${req.user.organizationName || req.user.name} accepted your donation "${accepted.foodName}".`,
    type: 'SUCCESS',
    relatedDonationId: accepted._id,
  });

  return ok(res, { donation: accepted }, 'Donation accepted successfully');

+# API Documentation — Community Food Donation and Distribution System
+
+Base URL (development): `http://localhost:5000/api`
+The React dev server proxies `/api` and `/uploads` to this address, so browser calls
+use the same origin (httpOnly cookies work without CORS configuration).
+
+---
+
+## 1. Conventions
+
+### Response envelope
+
+Every endpoint returns the same JSON shape:
+
+```json
+{
+  "success": true,
+  "message": "Human readable message",
+  "data": { ... }
+}
+```
+
+Errors:
+
+```json
+{
+  "success": false,
+  "message": "What went wrong",
+  "errors": { "field": ["Validation message"] }
+}
+```
+
+HTTP status codes: `200` OK · `201` Created · `400` validation/invalid transition ·
+`401` not authenticated · `403` not authorized · `404` not found ·
+`409` conflict (e.g. donation already accepted) · `429` rate limited.
+
+### Authentication
+
+- Login sets an **httpOnly cookie** (`cfds_token` by default) — the browser sends it automatically.
+- For API tools (Postman, curl) you can instead send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
+- Public list/detail endpoints use *optional* auth: admins see more (e.g. expired donations).
+
+### Roles
+
+`DONOR`, `NGO`, `VOLUNTEER`, `ADMIN`. Every protected route enforces its role on the
+**backend** (`protect` + `authorize` middleware). The admin role cannot be self-registered.
+
+### Reference data
+
+`GET /api/meta` returns all enums used by the forms/filters:
+food categories, units, classifications, donor categories, donation/pickup statuses,
+and the allowed registration roles.
+
+`GET /api/stats/public` returns landing-page statistics **counted from the database**
+(total donations, completed, NGOs, active volunteers) — never fabricated.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Status Lifecycle
+
+Donation status state machine (server-validated; illegal transitions are rejected):
+
+```
+AVAILABLE → ACCEPTED → PICKUP_ASSIGNED → COLLECTED → DISTRIBUTED → COMPLETED
+     ↘ CANCELLED / REJECTED (donor cancel or admin reject)
+```
+
+Pickup status: `OPEN → ASSIGNED → COLLECTED → DELIVERED → CONFIRMED` (or `CANCELLED`).
+
+Rules enforced server-side:
+- Only `AVAILABLE` donations **whose safe-consumption deadline has not passed** are eligible for acceptance.
+- A donation can be accepted by **one NGO only** — a second attempt returns `409 Conflict`.
+- `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`, `REJECTED` are terminal states.
+
+---
+
+## 3. Authentication — `/api/auth`
+
+| Method | Path | Access | Description |
+|--------|------|--------|-------------|
+| POST | `/register` | Public | Register a DONOR / NGO / VOLUNTEER account |
+| POST | `/login` | Public | Sign in (rate limited) |
+| POST | `/logout` | Any | Clear the session cookie |
+| GET | `/me` | Logged in | Current user profile |
+
+**POST /register** body:
+`name` (2–100), `email`, `password` (strong password required), `phone`,
+`role` (`DONOR` | `NGO` | `VOLUNTEER` — **not** `ADMIN`), `city`, optional `address`,
+`organizationName`, `organizationDescription`, `donorCategory`
+(Household, Restaurant, Hotel, Hostel, College Canteen, Event Organizer, Catering Service, Other),
+`terms: true`.
+
+NGO accounts are created with `verificationStatus: PENDING` (set to `VERIFIED` by an admin).
+Set `NGO_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION=true` to block PENDING NGOs from accepting donations.
+
+**POST /login** body: `email`, `password`. Returns the user profile; sets the session cookie.
+Wrong email and wrong password return the same generic `401` message.
+
+---
+
+## 4. Donations — `/api/donations`
+
+| Method | Path | Access | Description |
+|--------|------|--------|-------------|
+| GET | `/` | Public (optional auth) | List donations (anonymous = only AVAILABLE & not expired) |
+| GET | `/my` | DONOR | The logged-in donor's donations |
+| GET | `/:id` | Public (optional auth) | Donation details |
+| GET | `/:id/history` | Logged in (owner/NGO/volunteer/admin) | Full audit trail |
+| POST | `/` | DONOR | Create a donation (multipart: optional `image` + fields) |
+| PUT | `/:id` | DONOR (owner, only before acceptance) | Edit a donation |
+| PATCH | `/:id/cancel` | DONOR (owner, eligible states) | Cancel a donation |
+
+**GET / query parameters** (shared by the public page, NGO browse and admin table):
+
+| Param | Meaning |
+|-------|---------|
+| `status` | Filter by donation status (admins only see arbitrary statuses) |
+| `category` | Exact food category (Cooked Meals, Fruits, Vegetables, Bakery Products, Packaged Food, Rice and Grains, Other) |
+| `city` / `cityPartial` | Exact / partial city match (case-insensitive) |
+| `classification` | `VEG`, `NON_VEG`, `BOTH` |
+| `minQuantity`, `maxQuantity` | Quantity range |
+| `deadlineBefore` | ISO date — deadline must be before this |
+| `search` | Free text over food name, description, city, category |
+| `sort` | `newest`, `oldest`, `deadline`, `deadline-desc`, `quantity`, `name` |
+| `page`, `limit` | Pagination (returns `pagination: { page, limit, total, pages }`) |
+
+**POST / body** (validation in parentheses):
+`foodName` (≤120, required), `category` (enum, required), `description` (≤2000),
+`quantity` (>0, required), `unit` (Servings, Kg, Plates, Packs, Boxes, Litres, Dozen),
+`foodClassification` (VEG/NON_VEG/BOTH), `preparationDate`, `availableFrom`,
+`safeConsumptionDeadline` (ISO date, **required**),
+`pickupAddress`, `city`, `contactName`, `contactPhone`, optional `locationDescription`,
+`storageInformation`, `additionalNotes`, optional `image` (file ≤ 2 MB).
+
+Public list responses **never expose** donor identity/contact details.
+
+---
+
+## 5. NGO — `/api/ngo` (role: NGO)
+
+| Method | Path | Description |
+|--------|------|-------------|
+| GET | `/dashboard` | NGO counters + recent activity |
+| GET | `/donations` | Browse **available** donations (same filter params as `/api/donations`) |
+| GET | `/accepted-donations` | Donations accepted by this NGO |
+| POST | `/donations/:id/accept` | Accept an available, non-expired donation (`409` if taken) |
+| POST | `/donations/:id/request-volunteer` | Create/find the pickup task and optionally assign a specific volunteer |
+| PATCH | `/donations/:id/release-volunteer` | Release the assigned volunteer (task back to OPEN) |
+| PATCH | `/donations/:id/confirm-distribution` | Confirm distribution — donation becomes `COMPLETED` |
+
+`request-volunteer` body (all optional): `volunteerId` (Mongo id),
+`scheduledPickupTime` (ISO), `notes` (≤1000).
+`confirm-distribution` body (optional): `distributionNote` (≤500).
+
+---
+
+## 6. Volunteer — `/api/volunteer` (role: VOLUNTEER)
+
+| Method | Path | Description |
+|--------|------|-------------|
+| GET | `/dashboard` | Volunteer counters + recent activity |
+| GET | `/tasks` | Open pickup tasks (status OPEN) |
+| GET | `/tasks/my` | Tasks assigned to this volunteer |
+| GET | `/tasks/:id` | Task details (owner only) |
+| POST | `/tasks/:id/accept` | Accept an open task → pickup `ASSIGNED`, donation `PICKUP_ASSIGNED` |
+| PATCH | `/tasks/:id/collect` | Confirm collection (`notes` ≤1000) → donation `COLLECTED` |
+| PATCH | `/tasks/:id/deliver` | Confirm delivery (`deliveryNotes` ≤1000) → donation `DISTRIBUTED` |
+
+Volunteers cannot read or modify tasks assigned to another volunteer (`403`).
+
+---
+
+## 7. Admin — `/api/admin` (role: ADMIN)
+
+| Method | Path | Description |
+|--------|------|-------------|
+| GET | `/dashboard` | User/donation counters and recent activity (all DB-derived) |
+| GET | `/users` | Registered users (filters: `role`, `search`, `status`, pagination) |
+| GET | `/donations` | All donations (filters incl. `includeExpired=true`) |
+| GET | `/reports` | Report aggregates for the charts (by status/category, per-month series) |
+| PATCH | `/users/:id/status` | Body `{ isActive: true|false }` — activate/deactivate an account |
+| PATCH | `/ngos/:id/verify` | Body `{ verificationStatus: "VERIFIED"\|"REJECTED", note? }` |
+
+---
+
+## 8. Notifications — `/api`
+
+| Method | Path | Access | Description |
+|--------|------|--------|-------------|
+| GET | `/notifications` | Logged in | List the user's notifications |
+| PATCH | `/notifications/:id/read` | Logged in | Mark one as read |
+| PATCH | `/notifications/read-all` | Logged in | Mark all as read |
+
+Notifications are created automatically when a donation is accepted, a volunteer is
+assigned/collected/delivered, distribution is confirmed, an NGO is verified, etc.
+
+---
+
+## 9. System — `/api`
+
+| Method | Path | Access | Description |
+|--------|------|--------|-------------|
+| GET | `/health` | Public | `{ success, data: { uptime } }` |
+| GET | `/meta` | Public | Enum/reference data for forms |
+| GET | `/stats/public` | Public | Landing-page statistics (real DB counts) |
+
+---
+
+## 10. Example requests (curl)
+
+```bash
+# Login (cookie jar)
+curl -s -c cookies.txt -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{"email":"donor@cfds.local","password":"Demo@123"}' \
+  http://localhost:5000/api/auth/login
+
+# Create a donation with the cookie
+curl -s -b cookies.txt -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{"foodName":"Veg Pulao","category":"Cooked Meals","quantity":40,"unit":"Servings",
+       "safeConsumptionDeadline":"2027-01-01T18:00:00.000Z",
+       "pickupAddress":"12 MG Road","city":"Pune",
+       "contactName":"Ravi","contactPhone":"9876543210"}' \
+  http://localhost:5000/api/donations
+
+# Bearer-token style (Postman friendly)
+curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:5000/api/donations/my
+
+# NGO accepts (409 if another NGO already accepted)
+curl -s -b ngo-cookies.txt -X POST http://localhost:5000/api/ngo/donations/<ID>/accept
+```
+
+Rate limits: auth routes are limited (per 15 min); a global API limit defaults to
+600 requests/15 min (`API_RATE_LIMIT`).

+# Database Design — Community Food Donation and Distribution System
+
+Database: **MongoDB** (document store) accessed through **Mongoose ODM**.
+If `MONGODB_URI` is empty the server boots a temporary in-memory MongoDB for
+development/demos — the same schemas and queries are used unchanged.
+
+---
+
+## 1. Entity Relationship Overview
+
+```
+User (DONOR) 1 ──── * Donation * ──── 1 User (NGO)
+                      │  │
+                      │  └─────── * ──── 1 User (VOLUNTEER)   (assignedVolunteerId)
+                      │
+                      ├──── 1 Pickup (1 active per donation)
+                      │        └── volunteerId → User (VOLUNTEER)
+                      │
+                      └──── * DonationHistory  (immutable audit trail)
+
+User 1 ──── * Notification   (per-recipient in-app notifications)
+```
+
+Five collections (Mongoose models):
+
+| Model | File | Purpose |
+|-------|------|---------|
+| `User` | `server/models/User.js` | All four roles in one collection, discriminated by `role` |
+| `Donation` | `server/models/Donation.js` | A surplus-food listing and its lifecycle state |
+| `Pickup` | `server/models/Pickup.js` | Pickup/delivery task linking a donation, NGO and volunteer |
+| `DonationHistory` | `server/models/DonationHistory.js` | Append-only audit trail of every status change |
+| `Notification` | `server/models/Notification.js` | In-app notifications per user |
+
+---
+
+## 2. Collections
+
+### 2.1 `users`
+
+One collection for every role; `role` selects which optional profile fields matter.
+
+| Field | Type | Notes |
+|-------|------|-------|
+| `name` | String | 2–100 chars |
+| `email` | String | unique, lowercase, indexed |
+| `passwordHash` | String | bcrypt, **`select: false`**, stripped in `toJSON` |
+| `phone` | String | validated pattern |
+| `role` | String enum | `DONOR`, `NGO`, `VOLUNTEER`, `ADMIN` |
+| `address` | String | optional |
+| `city` | String | required, indexed with role |
+| `organizationName` | String | NGO profile |
+| `organizationDescription` | String | NGO profile |
+| `verificationStatus` | String enum | `NOT_REQUIRED`, `PENDING`, `VERIFIED`, `REJECTED` — NGOs start `PENDING` |
+| `verificationNote` | String | admin's note when verifying/rejecting |
+| `donorCategory` | String enum | Household, Restaurant, Hotel, Hostel, College Canteen, Event Organizer, Catering Service, Other |
+| `isActive` | Boolean | admin can deactivate an account (login and access blocked) |
+| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | Date | Mongoose timestamps |
+
+Indexes: `{ email: 1 }` (unique), `{ city: 1, role: 1 }`, `{ role: 1, isActive: 1 }`.
+
+### 2.2 `donations`
+
+| Field | Type | Notes |
+|-------|------|-------|
+| `foodName` | String | ≤120 |
+| `category` | String enum | Cooked Meals, Fruits, Vegetables, Bakery Products, Packaged Food, Rice and Grains, Other |
+| `description` | String | ≤2000 |
+| `quantity` | Number | >0 |
+| `unit` | String enum | Servings, Kg, Plates, Packs, Boxes, Litres, Dozen |
+| `foodClassification` | String enum | `VEG`, `NON_VEG`, `BOTH` |
+| `preparationDate` | Date | when the food was prepared |
+| `availableFrom` | Date | when pickup can start |
+| `safeConsumptionDeadline` | Date | **required** — expired donations are never eligible for acceptance |
+| `pickupAddress`, `city` | String | required pickup location |
+| `locationDescription` | String | landmarks etc. |
+| `storageInformation` | String | how the food is stored |
+| `additionalNotes` | String | free text |
+| `contactName`, `contactPhone` | String | required contact details |
+| `imageUrl` | String | Multer upload path (optional) |
+| `donorId` | ObjectId → User | required, indexed |
+| `acceptedByNgoId` | ObjectId → User | set on acceptance; guarantees single-NGO acceptance |
+| `assignedVolunteerId` | ObjectId → User | set when a volunteer takes the task |
+| `status` | String enum | see lifecycle below; default `AVAILABLE` |
+| `statusUpdatedAt` | Date | last transition time |
+| `statusUpdatedBy` | ObjectId → User | who made the last transition |
+
+Notes recorded during the flow (NGO distribution note, cancellation reason) are stored
+on the `Pickup` task and in the `DonationHistory` entry, keeping the donation document lean.
+
+Status lifecycle (`server/utils/statusFlow.js` — single source of truth, validated on
+every transition):
+
+```
+AVAILABLE → ACCEPTED → PICKUP_ASSIGNED → COLLECTED → DISTRIBUTED → COMPLETED
+     ↘ CANCELLED / REJECTED
+```
+
+`COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`, `REJECTED` are terminal. Acceptance eligibility =
+`status === AVAILABLE` **and** `safeConsumptionDeadline >= now`.
+
+Indexes: `{ status: 1, safeConsumptionDeadline: 1 }`, `{ city: 1, category: 1 }`,
+`{ donorId: 1, createdAt: -1 }` and a text index on `foodName / description / city`
+for free-text search.
+
+Concurrency safety: every status change goes through `services/donationStatusService.js`,
+which performs an atomic conditional update (`findOneAndUpdate` with the *expected current
+status* in the filter). If another NGO got there first, the update matches nothing and the
+request receives `409 Conflict` — two NGOs can never accept the same donation.
+
+### 2.3 `pickups`
+
+One **active** pickup task per donation (`isActive: true`); released volunteers
+return the task to `OPEN`.
+
+| Field | Type | Notes |
+|-------|------|-------|
+| `donationId` | ObjectId → Donation | required, indexed |
+| `ngoId` | ObjectId → User | the accepting NGO |
+| `volunteerId` | ObjectId → User | nullable until a volunteer accepts |
+| `pickupAddress`, `deliveryAddress` | String | copied from the donation / NGO profile |
+| `scheduledPickupTime` | Date | optional |
+| `assignmentDate` | Date | default now |
+| `status` | String enum | `OPEN`, `ASSIGNED`, `COLLECTED`, `DELIVERED`, `CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED` |
+| `collectedAt`, `deliveredAt`, `confirmedAt` | Date | event timestamps |
+| `notes` | String | volunteer's collection notes |
+| `deliveryNotes` | String | volunteer's delivery notes |
+| `isActive` | Boolean | one active task per donation |
+
+Index: **unique partial** on `{ donationId: 1 }` with `isActive: true` — the database
+itself guarantees at most one active pickup task per donation.
+
+The pickup status mirrors the donation status (collect → `COLLECTED` on both,
+deliver → donation `DISTRIBUTED`, NGO confirm → pickup `CONFIRMED` + donation `COMPLETED`).
+
+### 2.4 `donationhistories`
+
+Append-only audit trail — rows are **never updated or deleted**.
+
+| Field | Type | Notes |
+|-------|------|-------|
+| `donationId` | ObjectId → Donation | required, indexed |
+| `previousStatus` | String | null for the first entry |
+| `newStatus` | String | required |
+| `updatedBy` | ObjectId → User | who performed the transition |
+| `updatedByRole` | String | snapshot for easy filtering |
+| `note` | String | optional context (delivery notes, admin reason…) |
+| `timestamp` | Date | default now |
+
+Index: `{ donationId: 1, timestamp: -1 }`.
+The donor, NGO and admin detail pages all render this trail, so every status change
+is fully traceable — key for the platform's accountability goal.
+
+### 2.5 `notifications`
+
+| Field | Type | Notes |
+|-------|------|-------|
+| `recipientId` | ObjectId → User | recipient, indexed |
+| `title` | String | ≤120 |
+| `message` | String | ≤500 |
+| `type` | String enum | `INFO`, `SUCCESS`, `WARNING`, `DONATION`, `PICKUP`, `ACCOUNT` |
+| `relatedDonationId` | ObjectId → Donation | nullable deep link |
+| `isRead` | Boolean | default false, indexed |
+
+Indexes: `{ recipientId: 1 }`, `{ isRead: 1 }`, `{ recipientId: 1, createdAt: -1 }`.
+
+---
+
+## 3. Design Decisions
+
+1. **Single `users` collection** — the four roles share authentication/profile fields;
+   role-specific data lives in optional fields. Simple for a student project, and
+   querying "all NGOs in Pune" is one indexed query.
+2. **Status as data, transitions as code** — the state machine lives in
+   `utils/statusFlow.js`; controllers validate every transition against it, so an
+   illegal jump (e.g. `COMPLETED → AVAILABLE`) is impossible regardless of the caller.
+3. **Immutable audit trail** — `donationhistories` is insert-only; the current state
+   lives on the donation, the story lives in the trail.
+4. **Atomic transitions** — the shared `transitionDonation` service uses conditional
+   `findOneAndUpdate` on the expected current status, preventing the classic
+   double-accept race without distributed locks.
+5. **Denormalized pickup copy** — pickup/delivery addresses are copied onto the task
+   so the volunteer sees exactly what the donor registered even if the listing changes.
+6. **DB-level task uniqueness** — the partial unique index on `pickups { donationId, isActive: true }`
+   means even a bug in application code cannot create two active tasks for one donation.
+7. **Security by default** — `passwordHash` is `select: false`, stripped from JSON
+   output, and never returned by any endpoint.

+# Community Food Donation and Distribution System
+
+A full-stack web platform that reduces food wastage by connecting people and organizations
+with surplus food to NGOs and volunteers who collect and distribute it to people in need.
+
+Built as a B.Tech Computer Science Engineering **Community Service Project (CSP)**.
+
+**Core workflow:**
+Food Donor → Donation Registration → Verification → NGO Acceptance → Volunteer Assignment →
+Food Pickup → Distribution → Status Updates → Completion
+
+---
+
+## 1. Technology Stack
+
+| Layer     | Technology |
+|-----------|------------|
+| Frontend  | React 18 + Vite, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, React Router DOM, Axios, Recharts, Lucide React |
+| Backend   | Node.js + Express (REST API), JWT auth (httpOnly cookies + Bearer), bcryptjs, express-validator, express-rate-limit, Multer |
+| Database  | MongoDB + Mongoose ODM (falls back to a temporary **in-memory MongoDB** when `MONGODB_URI` is empty — ideal for demos without installing MongoDB) |
+| Testing   | Node.js built-in test runner (65 API tests) + an end-to-end smoke script (29 live checks) |
+
+Everything is free and open-source. No paid services are used.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Project Structure
+
+```
+.
+├── client/                     # React frontend (Vite)
+│   ├── index.html
+│   ├── vite.config.js          # dev proxy: /api and /uploads -> http://localhost:5000
+│   ├── .env.example
+│   └── src/
+│       ├── main.jsx            # entry point
+│       ├── App.jsx             # all routes for the four roles
+│       ├── index.css           # design system (Tailwind + theme tokens)
+│       ├── components/         # Navbar, Footer, cards, badges, dialogs, tables…
+│       ├── contexts/           # AuthContext, ToastContext
+│       ├── layouts/            # PublicLayout, DashboardLayout (sidebar shell)
+│       ├── pages/
+│       │   ├── Home.jsx  About.jsx  HowItWorks.jsx
+│       │   ├── AvailableDonations.jsx  DonationDetail.jsx
+│       │   ├── Login.jsx  Register.jsx
+│       │   ├── donor/          # dashboard, add/edit donation, list, history
+│       │   ├── ngo/            # dashboard, browse, accepted, history
+│       │   ├── volunteer/      # dashboard, open tasks, my tasks
+│       │   └── admin/          # dashboard, users, donations, reports & charts
+│       ├── services/api.js     # Axios instance + typed API helpers
+│       └── utils/
+│
+└── server/                     # Express backend
+    ├── server.js               # app wiring, static /uploads, DB connect, auto-seed
+    ├── .env.example
+    ├── config/db.js            # Mongoose connect (or in-memory MongoDB)
+    ├── middleware/             # auth (JWT), authorize, validate, upload, errorHandler
+    ├── models/                 # User, Donation, Pickup, DonationHistory, Notification
+    ├── controllers/            # auth, donations, ngo, volunteer, admin
+    ├── routes/                 # /api/auth, /api/donations, /api/ngo, /api/volunteer, /api/admin
+    ├── utils/statusFlow.js     # single source of truth for the status state machine
+    ├── scripts/
+    │   ├── seed.js             # demo data (npm run seed; server auto-seeds in-memory DB)
+    │   ├── createAdmin.js      # secure admin creation (npm run create-admin)
+    │   └── e2e-smoke.js        # 29-check live end-to-end workflow test
+    ├── uploads/                # uploaded food images (served statically)
+    └── tests/                  # 65 automated API tests
+```
+
+---
+
+## 3. Getting Started
+
+### Prerequisites
+- **Node.js 18+**
+- MongoDB (optional — see the in-memory note below)
+
+### 1) Backend
+
+```bash
+cd server
+npm install
+copy .env.example .env       # Windows   (cp .env.example .env on macOS/Linux)
+npm start                    # http://localhost:5000
+```
+
+Useful scripts:
+
+```bash
+npm run dev          # auto-restart on changes (node --watch)
+npm run seed         # load demo users + donations into MongoDB
+npm run create-admin # create/reuse the administrator account (interactive)
+npm test             # 65 automated API tests
+node scripts/e2e-smoke.js http://localhost:5173   # 29 live end-to-end checks
+```
+
+**No MongoDB?** Leave `MONGODB_URI=` empty in `server/.env`. The server starts a
+temporary in-memory MongoDB, **auto-seeds** the demo data and runs the whole application.
+All data is lost when the server stops — perfect for presentations.
+
+### 2) Frontend
+
+```bash
+cd client
+npm install
+npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173
+```
+
+The Vite dev server proxies `/api` and `/uploads` to `http://localhost:5000`, so the
+browser talks to a single origin and httpOnly auth cookies work out of the box.
+
+### 3) Production build
+
+```bash
+cd client && npm run build     # static files in client/dist
+cd server && npm start         # serves the API; mount client/dist behind a reverse proxy
+```
+
+---
+
+## 4. Environment Configuration
+
+### `server/.env`
+
+| Variable | Purpose | Default |
+|----------|---------|---------|
+| `PORT` | API port | `5000` |
+| `MONGODB_URI` | MongoDB connection string. **Empty = in-memory DB (dev/demo)** | empty |
+| `JWT_SECRET` | Secret for signing JWTs — use a long random string | — |
+| `JWT_EXPIRES_IN` | Session lifetime | `1d` |
+| `JWT_COOKIE_NAME` | Name of the httpOnly cookie | `cfds_token` |
+| `CLIENT_ORIGINS` | CORS allow-list (comma separated) | `http://localhost:5173,...` |
+| `NGO_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION` | Require admin verification before an NGO can accept | `false` |
+| `API_RATE_LIMIT` | Global API limit per 15 min | `600` |
+| `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES` | Max food-image upload size | `2097152` (2 MB) |
+| `NODE_ENV` | `development` / `production` / `test` | `development` |
+
+### `client/.env`
+
+| Variable | Purpose |
+|----------|---------|
+| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | Empty = use the Vite proxy (recommended). Set an absolute URL to call the API on another origin (then add the frontend to `CLIENT_ORIGINS`). |
+
+---
+
+## 5. Demo Accounts
+
+The seed data creates these accounts — **password for all: `Demo@123`**
+(`npm run seed`, or automatically at first start when using the in-memory DB):
+
+| Role | Email |
+|------|-------|
+| Administrator | `admin@cfds.local` |
+| Donor (household) | `donor@cfds.local` |
+| Donor (restaurant) | `restaurant@cfds.local` |
+| NGO (verified) | `ngo@cfds.local` |
+| NGO (verified) | `ngo2@cfds.local` |
+| Volunteer | `volunteer@cfds.local` |
+| Volunteer | `volunteer2@cfds.local` |
+
+### Creating the administrator securely
+
+There is **no public admin registration page**. Create the admin account with:
+
+```bash
+cd server
+npm run create-admin     # prompts for name, email, password (or pass CLI arguments)
+```
+
+The script refuses weak passwords, never prints the password, and is safe to re-run
+(it reuses the existing admin account). See `server/scripts/createAdmin.js`.
+
+---
+
+## 6. Implemented Features
+
+### Food Donor
+- Register/login, choose a donor category (Household, Restaurant, Hotel, Hostel, College Canteen, Event Organizer, Catering Service, Other)
+- Personal dashboard with live counters and recent activity
+- Create donations: food name/description, category, quantity + unit, preparation/availability times, **safe-consumption deadline**, pickup address/city, contact details, optional image upload (Multer)
+- Food-safety notice on the donation form; expired donations are never eligible for acceptance
+- Edit donations not yet accepted; cancel eligible donations; full donation history
+
+### NGO
+- Register (organization name, address, phone, description) — new NGOs start `PENDING`
+- Browse available donations; search by text; filter by category, city, quantity and deadline
+- Accept an available donation — **concurrency-safe**: a second NGO gets `409 Conflict`
+- View accepted donations, request/release a volunteer, track pickup and distribution status
+- Confirm distribution (moves the donation to `COMPLETED`)
+- Completed donation history
+
+### Volunteer
+- Register with contact details and location
+- View open pickup tasks and full pickup/delivery details
+- Accept an eligible task, confirm collection, confirm delivery, add delivery notes
+- "My tasks" list — volunteers cannot see or touch tasks assigned to other volunteers
+- Completed task history
+
+### Administrator
+- Protected dashboard: total users, donors, NGOs, volunteers, donations, and status counters (pending / accepted / collected / distributed / completed / cancelled) — **all computed from database records**
+- User management: activate/deactivate accounts, verify or reject NGO registrations
+- Donation monitoring with status filters and per-donation audit trail
+- Reports page with charts (Recharts): donations by status, by category, per-month trend, user registrations per month
+- Recent platform activity
+
+### Platform
+- JWT auth in **httpOnly cookies** (Bearer tokens also accepted for API tools like Postman)
+- Role-based authorization middleware enforced on **every** protected route (backend is the authority)
+- Donation status state machine with server-side validation of every transition
+- Immutable `DonationHistory` audit trail for every status change
+- In-app notifications (list, mark read, mark all read)
+- Public stats endpoint (real counts, no fabricated numbers)
+- Rate limiting on auth routes, request validation with express-validator, centralized error handler
+- Responsive UI, empty states, loading spinners, toasts, confirmation dialogs, status badges
+
+---
+
+## 7. Testing
+
+```bash
+cd server
+npm test                            # 65 automated API tests (auth, CRUD, workflow, authz)
+node scripts/e2e-smoke.js http://localhost:5173   # 29 live end-to-end checks
+```
+
+The smoke script drives the **complete acceptance workflow** with real HTTP requests
+through the Vite proxy (exactly what the browser does):
+
+1. Donor logs in and creates a donation → appears in the public list (donor contact hidden)
+2. NGO 1 accepts; NGO 2 is rejected with `409`
+3. Volunteer accepts the pickup, confirms collection, confirms delivery
+4. NGO confirms distribution → donation reaches `COMPLETED`; double-confirm rejected
+5. Donor sees `COMPLETED`; audit trail is complete
+6. Admin counters match the database; admin can open the donation history
+7. Authorization matrix: anonymous/donor/volunteer against admin & NGO routes → `401/403`;
+   wrong password rejected; ADMIN self-registration rejected
+
+**Latest results: 65/65 unit tests pass, 29/29 live end-to-end checks pass.**
+
+Manual browser checks performed: Home (live stats), Login → Donor dashboard,
+Admin dashboard with Recharts, responsive navigation — no console errors.
+
+---
+
+## 8. API & Database Documentation
+
+- REST API reference: [API_DOCUMENTATION.md](API_DOCUMENTATION.md)
+- Schema design & relationships: [DATABASE_DESIGN.md](DATABASE_DESIGN.md)
+
+---
+
+## 9. Optional / Future Enhancements
+
+Not required for the demo, but natural next steps:
+
+- Email/SMS notifications with Nodemailer (the `Notification` model already stores everything needed)
+- Maps/geolocation for nearby NGO–volunteer matching
+- Image resizing/optimization and cloud storage for uploads
+- Refresh tokens and per-device session management
+- E2E browser tests (Playwright) automating the smoke workflow
+- Docker Compose for one-command setup with real MongoDB
+
+## 10. Known Limitations
+
+- With an empty `MONGODB_URI`, data lives in memory and is lost on server restart (by design — the seed data is re-created automatically).
+- Food images are stored on local disk (`server/uploads/`); use a real filesystem/volume in production.
+- Notifications are in-app only (no email delivery yet).

## What was done this session

- **Backend** (Express + MongoDB/Mongoose): JWT auth in httpOnly cookies (Bearer also works), 4-role authorization (`DONOR`/`NGO`/`VOLUNTEER`/`ADMIN`) enforced server-side on every route, 5 models (User, Donation, Pickup, DonationHistory, Notification), a validated status state machine (`AVAILABLE → ACCEPTED → PICKUP_ASSIGNED → COLLECTED → DISTRIBUTED → COMPLETED`) with atomic, race-safe NGO acceptance, an immutable audit trail, in-app notifications, image uploads (Multer), rate limiting, and DB-derived stats.
- **Frontend** (React + Vite + Tailwind + Recharts): public pages (Home with live stats, About, How It Works, Available Donations, Donation Detail, Login, Register) plus full dashboards for all four roles — donor CRUD with food-safety/expiry rules, NGO browse/filter/accept/request-volunteer/confirm-distribution, volunteer task acceptance with collection/delivery updates, and an admin panel with user management, NGO verification, donation monitoring and charts.


- With an empty `MONGODB_URI`, data is in-memory (lost on restart, auto re-seeded) — by design for demos; set a real URI for persistence.

## Database config

`server/config/db.js`:
- If `MONGODB_URI` is set → connects to that (local or **MongoDB Atlas**).
- If empty → boots an **in-memory MongoDB**, auto-seeds demo data, **wipes on restart**. This is for demos only — **it will not work in production** (`NODE_ENV=production` throws if `MONGODB_URI` is unset).

Models: `User`, `Donation`, `Pickup`, `DonationHistory`, `Notification`.

## Environment variables you must set (backend)

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `MONGODB_URI` | **Yes (prod)** | Atlas SRV string. Empty = in-memory (data loss). |
| `JWT_SECRET` | **Yes** | Server refuses to boot without it. |
| `CLIENT_ORIGINS` | **Yes** | Comma-separated. **Must include your live frontend URL** or CORS blocks cookies. |
| `PORT` | No | Defaults to 5000; hosts usually inject their own. |
| `NODE_ENV` | **Yes** | `production`. |
| `JWT_EXPIRES_IN` | No | default `1d` |
| `JWT_COOKIE_NAME` | No | default `cfds_token` |
| `API_RATE_LIMIT` | No | default 600 / 15min |
| `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES` | No | default 2 MB |
| `NGO_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION` | No | default false |

The frontend reads only `VITE_API_BASE_URL` (empty = use proxy; set = call API directly, and that origin's host must be in `CLIENT_ORIGINS`).

## Two things that will break your live site if ignored

1. **Cookies are httpOnly + `withCredentials: true`.** The frontend and backend must be reachable such that the browser accepts the cookie. Cross-origin works only if `CLIENT_ORIGINS` lists the exact frontend origin (scheme + host, no trailing slash) *and* the backend returns `SameSite=None; Secure`. Your `server/.env` and the deployed frontend URL matter here.
2. **Image uploads use local disk (`server/uploads/`)** and Multer. Most PaaS disks are **ephemeral** — uploaded images vanish on redeploy. Needs a volume or cloud storage (e.g. S3/Cloudinary) for a durable production setup.

The frontend is now correctly wired to your Render backend, and I found and fixed the one place that would have broken on the live site. Everything is verified locally; nothing is committed or deployed yet.

## What was already working (no change needed)
- **Backend CORS** already whitelists `https://freebuff-roan.vercel.app` — it returns `access-control-allow-origin` with credentials, and preflight passes. I verified this directly against your live backend.
- **Auth** works cross-origin: your frontend sends the JWT as a `Authorization: Bearer` header, and the backend's `protect` middleware accepts the cookie *or* the header ([auth.js:10-13](server/middleware/auth.js)). The `sameSite: 'lax'` cookie won't be sent cross-site, but the Bearer header covers it, so no backend change is required.

## The problem I found
The deployed Vercel bundle had `VITE_API_BASE_URL` empty at build time, so it was calling `https://freebuff-roan.vercel.app/api/...` — which returns **404** (Vercel serves only static files). In other words, the live frontend currently can't reach your backend at all. Additionally, uploaded food images use a root-relative `/uploads/...` URL that would resolve against Vercel and break.

## What I changed (frontend only, local — not deployed)
1. **[client/.env](client/.env)** — set `VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://food-donation-34al.onrender.com` so the build calls the Render API.
2. **[api.js](client/src/services/api.js)** — added a `resolveImageUrl` helper that prefixes relative `/uploads/...` paths with the API origin (no-op in local dev, where the Vite proxy serves `/uploads`).
3. **[DonationDetail.jsx](client/src/pages/DonationDetail.jsx)** — the only place that renders an uploaded image, now uses `resolveImageUrl`.

## Verified
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- The built bundle contains `https://food-donation-34al.onrender.com` and **no** `localhost:5000`.
- Backend `/api/health` → 200 and `/api/stats/public` returns real data.
- CORS preflight from the Vercel origin → 204 with all methods allowed.

## To go live (your call — I haven't committed or deployed)
Commit and push these three files, then redeploy on Vercel (or connect the repo so it auto-builds). Vercel must build `client/` with the env var available; since it's now committed in `.env`, the default `vite build` will pick it up:
```bash
git add client/.env client/src/services/api.js client/src/pages/DonationDetail.jsx
git commit -m "Point frontend at Render API and resolve image URLs"
git push
```
Then log in on the live site (`admin@cfds.local` / `Demo@123`) and confirm the dashboard loads and an image upload persists after a backend redeploy.

## Two caveats that remain (unchanged, worth knowing)
- **Uploaded images are stored on Render's local disk** (`server/uploads/`), which is ephemeral — they'll disappear on each backend redeploy. Durable images need cloud storage (S3/Cloudinary) or a Render persistent disk.
- **Cookie flag**: if you'd rather rely on httpOnly cookies than the Bearer header, the backend would need `sameSite: 'none'` + `secure: true` in production. Not required today since Bearer auth works.

Here are the deployment steps for your stack — **backend** (Node.js/Express + MongoDB) on **Render**, **frontend** (Vite/React) on **Vercel**, database on **MongoDB Atlas**. Your repo is `github.com/saijaswanth76/freebuff.git` with `server/` and `client/` folders.

## Step 1 — Database (MongoDB Atlas, free M0)

1. Create a free M0 cluster at cloud.mongodb.com.
2. Create a database user (username + password).
3. Under Network Access, allow `0.0.0.0/0` (or Render's IPs).
4. Copy the connection string — it looks like:
   `mongodb+srv://USER:PASSWORD@cluster0.xxxxx.mongodb.net/community_food_system`

⚠️ Leave `MONGODB_URI` empty only for local demos. Your code **throws on boot in production** if it's unset (`server/config/db.js`), and in-memory data is wiped every restart — Atlas is required.

## Step 2 — Backend on Render

1. Render → **New → Web Service** → connect your GitHub repo.
2. Settings:
   - **Root Directory:** `server`
   - **Build Command:** `npm install`
   - **Start Command:** `npm start`
   - **Instance Type:** Free (fine for demos; sleeps after inactivity)
3. **Environment** tab → add:

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `NODE_ENV` | `production` |
| `MONGODB_URI` | your Atlas SRV string |
| `JWT_SECRET` | long random: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('hex'))"` |
| `CLIENT_ORIGINS` | `https://YOUR-VERCEL-APP.vercel.app` |
| `NGO_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION` | `false` (or `true` if you want NGOs vetted) |

`PORT` is injected by Render automatically and your server reads it.

4. Create the admin account (no public admin registration exists):
   Render → Shell → `cd server && npm run create-admin`
   Then optionally seed demo data: `npm run seed`

## Step 3 — Frontend on Vercel

1. Vercel → **Add New Project** → import the same repo.
2. Settings:
   - **Root Directory:** `client`
   - **Framework Preset:** Vite
   - **Build Command:** `npm run build`
   - **Output Directory:** `dist`
3. **Environment Variables:**

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | `https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com` |

This must be a **build-time** variable — Vercel bakes it into the bundle when it builds. Note [client/.env](client/.env) currently has it empty (for local dev) and `.env` is gitignored, so the Vercel variable is the one that matters.

4. Deploy.

## Step 4 — Connect the two

- Backend `CLIENT_ORIGINS` must contain **exactly** the Vercel origin: `https://YOUR-VERCEL-APP.vercel.app` (scheme + host, no trailing slash, no path). Otherwise CORS blocks every request. Use your actual production domain (e.g. `https://food-donation-34al.onrender.com` for the backend) and your real Vercel URL.
- Re-render/redeploy the backend after changing env vars (Render does this automatically).

## Step 5 — Verify

```bash
# 1. Backend healthy?
curl https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com/api/health

# 2. CORS returns your frontend origin?
curl -s -i https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com/api/health \
  -H "Origin: https://YOUR-VERCEL-APP.vercel.app" | grep -i access-control-allow-origin
```

Then open the Vercel URL and check:

## Known production caveats

1. **Images are lost on redeploy** — uploads go to local disk (`server/uploads/`), which is ephemeral on Render. Fix later with a Render persistent disk or cloud storage (S3/Cloudinary).
2. **First request is slow** — Render free tier sleeps; the first hit takes ~30s, then it's warm.
3. **Cookies** — auth also works via the `Authorization: Bearer` header your frontend already sends, so cross-site login works even though the httpOnly cookie is `SameSite=Lax`.

Fixed. The donor dropdowns were rendering empty because every page loaded its options only from the async `/api/meta` call and initialized those lists as empty arrays — so until the request resolved (or forever, if it failed, which is likely on Render's cold starts), the "Donor category" and donation-form dropdowns showed no options.

**Root cause:** [Register.jsx](client/src/pages/Register.jsx), [AddDonation.jsx](client/src/pages/donor/AddDonation.jsx), [EditDonation.jsx](client/src/pages/donor/EditDonation.jsx), [AvailableDonations.jsx](client/src/pages/AvailableDonations.jsx), [NgoBrowse.jsx](client/src/pages/ngo/NgoBrowse.jsx), and [AdminDonations.jsx](client/src/pages/admin/AdminDonations.jsx) all did `useState({ foodCategories: [], ... })` and `.map()` over those empty arrays.

**Fix:** added [metaFallbacks.js](client/src/utils/metaFallbacks.js) — static copies of the backend's option lists (food categories, units, donor categories) plus a `mergeMeta` helper. Each page now initializes its dropdowns from these fallbacks so they're populated on first render, and the live `/api/meta` values override them when they arrive. If the request fails, the fallbacks stay — the form never goes blank.

**Verified:** production build passes (`vite build`, 2294 modules, no errors); a source sweep confirms zero remaining empty-array initializations for these lists; and in the browser the `#donorCategory option` selector matched content after the change. Progress note:
Here are the deployment steps for your stack — **backend** (Node.js/Express + MongoDB) on **Render**, **frontend** (Vite/React) on **Vercel**, database on **MongoDB Atlas**. Your repo is `github.com/saijaswanth76/freebuff.git` with `server/` and `client/` folders.

## Step 1 — Database (MongoDB Atlas, free M0)

1. Create a free M0 cluster at cloud.mongodb.com.
2. Create a database user (username + password).
3. Under Network Access, allow `0.0.0.0/0` (or Render's IPs).
4. Copy the connection string — it looks like:
   `mongodb+srv://USER:PASSWORD@cluster0.xxxxx.mongodb.net/community_food_system`

⚠️ Leave `MONGODB_URI` empty only for local demos. Your code **throws on boot in production** if it's unset (`server/config/db.js`), and in-memory data is wiped every restart — Atlas is required.

## Step 2 — Backend on Render

1. Render → **New → Web Service** → connect your GitHub repo.
2. Settings:
   - **Root Directory:** `server`
   - **Build Command:** `npm install`
   - **Start Command:** `npm start`
   - **Instance Type:** Free (fine for demos; sleeps after inactivity)
3. **Environment** tab → add:

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `NODE_ENV` | `production` |
| `MONGODB_URI` | your Atlas SRV string |
| `JWT_SECRET` | long random: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('hex'))"` |
| `CLIENT_ORIGINS` | `https://YOUR-VERCEL-APP.vercel.app` |
| `NGO_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION` | `false` (or `true` if you want NGOs vetted) |

`PORT` is injected by Render automatically and your server reads it.

4. Create the admin account (no public admin registration exists):
   Render → Shell → `cd server && npm run create-admin`
   Then optionally seed demo data: `npm run seed`

## Step 3 — Frontend on Vercel

1. Vercel → **Add New Project** → import the same repo.
2. Settings:
   - **Root Directory:** `client`
   - **Framework Preset:** Vite
   - **Build Command:** `npm run build`
   - **Output Directory:** `dist`
3. **Environment Variables:**

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | `https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com` |

This must be a **build-time** variable — Vercel bakes it into the bundle when it builds. Note [client/.env](client/.env) currently has it empty (for local dev) and `.env` is gitignored, so the Vercel variable is the one that matters.

## Step 4 — Connect the two
